title: Bài sưu tầm 238 - Passage 2: Living Stone: How Bacteria Are Teaching Concrete to Repair Itself
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 238

Living Stone: How Bacteria Are Teaching Concrete to Repair Itself

Paragraph A. Concrete is the most widely manufactured material on Earth, yet it suffers from an unavoidable structural flaw: it cracks. As bridges flex under heavy lorries and tunnels cool after setting, microscopic fractures gradually appear. Inspection teams patch visible highways every summer, yet repair budgets cannot keep pace because hairline fissures expand out of sight beneath asphalt and decorative paint long before surface damage draws attention.

Paragraph B. On its own, a hair-thin crack rarely causes a structure to collapse immediately. The real danger begins when rain, road salt, and oxygen follow that pathway inward. Once water seeps down to the buried steel reinforcement, rust forms, swells outward, and splits the surrounding stone from within. Replacing corroded bridge decks prematurely costs public agencies billions each year and disrupts transport networks for months at a time.

Paragraph C. Looking to human bone—which heals minor fractures automatically—Dutch microbiologist Dr. Hendrik Jonkers wondered whether stone could borrow a similar biological trick. Ordinary concrete is harshly alkaline, making it hostile to almost all living cells. However, Jonkers turned to hardy Bacillus bacteria naturally found in soda lakes. By embedding dormant spores of these alkali-tolerant microbes directly into the wet mix, he created organisms capable of resting safely inside dry concrete for decades without food or oxygen. Only when a fresh fracture lets rainwater trickle inside do the resting cells wake up, dissolve their stored nutrient, and convert that feed into hardened limestone that gradually bridges the split.

Paragraph D. Turning this laboratory concept into a commercial product hit an early setback during factory mixing trials. Simply stirring raw sugar or calcium lactate powder straight into wet cement caused the mixture to lose compressive strength, while the added nutrient sharply pushed up production costs. To stop the food compound from reacting prematurely with cement paste—and to lower material waste—Jonkers’s team began sealing both bacteria and calcium lactate inside tiny porous clay pellets before blending. Those protective capsules stay intact until a passing crack snaps them open right where healing is needed.

Paragraph E. Real-world weather trials have started testing whether biological healing matches or surpasses conventional chemical repairs. On exposed concrete slabs in northern Europe, engineers compared bacterial mixes with standard waterproof resins over twenty-four months. While synthetic surface coatings cracked and peeled after two winters of salt and frost, the bio-concrete panels automatically sealed fissures up to half a millimetre wide within three weeks of rain. Still, engineers caution that biological healing cannot mend wide structural breaks caused by earthquakes or foundation subsidence.

Paragraph F. Beyond longer-lasting bridges and tunnels, self-healing mixes carry an important climate advantage. Heating limestone kilns to manufacture Portland cement currently accounts for roughly eight percent of global carbon dioxide output. Because structures built with bacterial capsules last significantly longer before needing demolition, reducing demand for fresh cement could cut industrial carbon emissions significantly, even before cleaner kiln fuels arrive.

Paragraph G. Cost remains the single biggest barrier keeping bio-concrete out of everyday housing. Because encapsulated bacterial additives still cost roughly fifty percent more per cubic metre than standard concrete, contractors currently reserve them for high-risk structures—such as marine seawalls, underground water tanks, and remote mountain tunnels—where sending human repair crews is far more expensive than paying extra upfront.

groups.title: Questions 14–18
groups.instructions:
Reading Passage 238 has seven sections, A–G.
Which section contains the following information?
Write the correct letter, A–G, in boxes 14–18 on your answer sheet.

groups.title: Questions 19–20
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Write the correct letters in boxes 19 and 20 on your answer sheet.
Which TWO conditions are required before embedded bacteria begin repairing a crack?
options: A. External steel bars must first be exposed to direct sunlight.
B. Moisture has to reach the sleeping organisms through the opening.
C. Ambient air temperatures must stay above thirty degrees Celsius.
D. A supplied nutrient needs to dissolve alongside the reviving microbes.
E. Maintenance crews have to inject fresh cement powder into the gap.

groups.title: Questions 21–26
groups.instructions:
Complete the summary below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 21–26 on your answer sheet.
groups.template:
Ordinary concrete develops tiny fractures over time, letting water seep down to internal steel 21. {{q21}} , which then expands as it rusts. To prevent this, microbiologist Dr. Hendrik Jonkers mixed tough bacterial 22. {{q22}} into wet cement.

Because raw nutrients can interfere with setting strength, the food compound is locked inside lightweight 23. {{q23}} granules before blending. When a fresh crack admits rain, the revived microbes consume the nutrient and produce solid 24. {{q24}} , sealing the gap. In cold-climate trials, this biological patch outperformed synthetic 25. {{q25}} that flaked off over winter. Beyond safer infrastructure, fewer replacements could shrink the massive 26. {{q26}} generated by traditional cement production.

q14.text: the reason routine maintenance often falls behind hidden structural decay

steps: Đoạn A: Các vết nứt mảnh lan rộng âm thầm dưới lớp nhựa đường và sơn trước khi đội bảo trì phát hiện trên bề mặt.
Kết luận: Chọn A.

q15.text: how dormant microbes remain alive inside an inhospitable building material for decades

steps: Đoạn C: Bào tử vi khuẩn ưa kiềm Bacillus ngủ yên an toàn bên trong bê tông khô suốt nhiều thập kỷ không cần thức ăn hay oxy.
Kết luận: Chọn C.

q16.text: a comparison showing how self-healing concrete performs alongside traditional surface treatments

steps: Đoạn E: Thử nghiệm 24 tháng đối chiếu lớp phủ nhựa chống thấm truyền thống (nứt bong sau 2 mùa đông) với bê tông vi khuẩn (tự bịt khe nứt).
Kết luận: Chọn E.

q17.text: an early manufacturing drawback that both weakened concrete and raised expenses

steps: Đoạn D: Trộn thẳng chất dinh dưỡng vào xi măng ướt làm giảm cường độ nén và đội chi phí.
Kết luận: Chọn D.

q18.text: an environmental benefit gained by reducing how often new cement is produced

steps: Đoạn F: Công trình bền hơn giúp giảm nhu cầu sản xuất xi măng mới, từ đó giảm khí thải CO2 từ lò nung.
Kết luận: Chọn F.

q19.text: Condition 1 for bacteria to begin repairing a crack

steps: Đoạn C: "Only when a fresh fracture lets rainwater trickle inside do the resting cells wake up..." → Độ ẩm phải chạm tới bào tử qua vết nứt (B).

q20.text: Condition 2 for bacteria to begin repairing a crack

steps: Đoạn C: "...dissolve their stored nutrient, and convert that feed into hardened limestone..." → Chất dinh dưỡng hòa tan cùng vi khuẩn thức dậy (D).
Đoạn B: "Once water seeps down to the buried steel reinforcement, rust forms..."
Từ cần điền: reinforcement.
Đoạn C: "By embedding dormant spores of these alkali-tolerant microbes directly into the wet mix..."
Từ cần điền: spores.
Đoạn D: "sealing both bacteria and calcium lactate inside tiny porous clay pellets..."
Từ cần điền: clay.
Đoạn C: "convert that feed into hardened limestone that gradually bridges the split."
Từ cần điền: limestone.
Đoạn E: "While synthetic surface coatings cracked and peeled after two winters..."
Từ cần điền: coatings.
Đoạn F: "reducing demand for fresh cement could cut industrial carbon emissions significantly..."
Từ cần điền: emissions.
